candidate.name: Non-Lapse Independent-Kinetic Screened Preferred-Frame
candidate.claimed_mechanism: The khronon u carries the preferred-frame response and is multiplied by e^-y, while the auxiliary scalar chi carries the propagating MOND mode with an independent finite kinetic coefficient. A multiplier lambda imposes a local algebraic constraint that fixes the screened preferred-frame coefficient without multiplying any term by the lapse or ln N. This removes the lapse-weighted flux structure that caused DC-003 while preserving the separation between screened preferred-frame coupling and propagating-mode kinetic normalization.
candidate.predicted_weak_field: In the weak-field, low-acceleration limit chi reproduces the frozen interpolation mu(y)=1-e^-y and gives the expected 1/r MOND scaling with a_0. The preferred-frame response is suppressed by e^-y in high-acceleration environments, so the effective alpha tends to zero where screening is strong. Because no lapse-weighted flux is present, the chi quadratic action remains O(1) and the propagating mode is finite in the screened regime.
candidate.inequivalence_argument: This candidate is inequivalent to DC-003 because every coupling has lapse_weighted=false and no term is a lapse-weighted flux, phi=lnN, or N-weighted MOND term; the multiplier constraint is algebraic in lambda, chi, and u and does not demote H_perp to three DOF or zero out the quadratic action. It is also not a coefficient tweak of a killed architecture, because the independent chi kinetic sector plus the algebraic constraint changes the canonical structure by decoupling the screened preferred-frame coefficient from the finite propagating-mode normalization. It satisfies the required lensing escape through the preferred_frame=true, screened_by=e^-y coupling.

kill_certificate.certificate: preferred-frame coupling with no e^-y screening (P2: AeST/disformal kill)
